    tables: [tab_1_temporal_landscape, tab_2_structural_comparison]
    figures: [fig_2_dose_response, fig_3_within_subject_matching, fig_4_downstream_impact, fig_5_gsm1k_dif_correlation]

  - section: discussion
    word_budget: 1000
    core_bullets:
      - >-
        5.1 Implications for benchmark temporal comparability: 31%
        instability (robust across thresholds: 10-49% at ETS 2.5-1.0)
        means cross-temporal MMLU scores carry uncontrolled item-level
        variance; instability decomposition shows 92.4% unrelated to
        domain accuracy improvement; benchmark designers should monitor
        DIF as quality diagnostic
      - >-
        5.2 Ground truth meta-critique — AGGRESSIVE framing per Director:
        all work validating item-level detectors against web-overlap/n-gram
        labels has the same validation methodology gap. Web-overlap measures
        existence, not differential usage. This is a meta-contribution to
        the contamination detection field — not just "DIF and Li et al.
        measure different things" but "the field's standard validation
        approach is fundamentally mismatched for item-level detection."
      - >-
        5.3a DIF as capability diagnostic (Claim 4 layer 4 discussion):
        GSM1K negative correlation reveals contamination produces "shallow"
        performance boost concentrated on non-DIF items, while DIF-C items
        capture genuine capability differences between model generations.
        171/249 focal-favoring DIF-C items (α<1) drive the effect — these
        are items where 2024 models genuinely improved, and contaminated
        models struggle disproportionately on them. MUST caveat: r=−0.478
        with CI=[−0.71, −0.16] is suggestive; item difficulty confound
        (DIF-C items may simply be harder) not fully excluded; N=33 limits
        generalizability. This is a paper highlight per Director but
        requires honest strength calibration.
      - >-
        5.3b Empirical observation on DIF applicability: 1D IRT fit
        limitations + power requirements + ability confounding jointly
        constrain DIF utility in LLM benchmarks. This is a structural
        constraint revealed by systematic experimentation, NOT a formal
        impossibility — higher-level methods (MIMIC, propensity-score
        matching, multidimensional IRT) may address individual constraints.
      - >-
        5.4 Limitations — MUST BE HONEST, non-negotiable:
        (a) ρ=0.307 ecological correlation between C% and accuracy
        improvement, but item-level decomposition (plan_019) shows
        domain improvement explains only 2.4pp (7.6%) of 31.3% C%.
        Still, cannot fully decompose remaining 92.4% into
        contamination vs other sources of capability change;
        (b) 38% C% cannot be decomposed into contamination vs capability;
        (c) semi-synthetic injection (incorrect→correct flipping) may
        not match real contamination patterns (partial knowledge, format
        memorization);
        (d) primarily MMLU/METABENCH — GSM8K cross-validation (§4.8)
        confirms semi-synthetic framework portability and provides GSM1K
        correlation evidence (N=33), but full temporal DIF characterization
        on diverse benchmarks not yet done; GSM1K N=33 has wide CI;
        (e) cross-subject baseline FPR 33-53% — stable across injection
        levels but not low;
        (f) RL robustness: theoretically motivated but empirically
        unvalidated with adequate sample size (N=13 reasoning-RL models
        in METABENCH);
        (g) downstream impact family analysis limited to N≥20 families
        (llama, mistral, qwen, phi); top-50 rank movers 49/50 are
        "unknown" family — family-level conclusions have limited coverage
      - >-
        5.5 Future work (SCOPE REDUCED per Dream #3 — main text only
        lists directions, no extended discussion): broader cross-
        benchmark generalization, RL model cohorts with adequate N,
        MIMIC models for confound control. [Appendix-only: Bayesian DIF,
        ensemble fusion (DIF + ConStat + DVD), complementary baselines,
        pilot studies (bifactor equating, item generation), SIBTEST/LR-DIF
        comparison, item-focused trees]
    dependencies: [experiments]

  - section: conclusion
    word_budget: 350
    core_bullets:
      - >-
        Four contributions: (1) 38% MMLU items functionally unstable
        across model generations, (2) ground truth meta-critique —
        validation methodology gap in contamination detection, (3)
        semi-synthetic framework with cross-subject matching (cross-
        benchmark replication on GSM8K: ΔTPR=+0.818), (4) DIF as
        diagnostic lens — four-layer finding
      - >-
        Key message: LLM benchmarks need psychometric monitoring, not
        just score reporting — DIF reveals benchmark quality as a
        benchmark quality tool
      - >-
        DIF items concentrate discriminative information (removal disrupts
        rankings MORE than random, z=-8 to -49σ) and anti-correlate with
        contamination gap (r=−0.478, CI=[−0.71, −0.16]) — DIF-C items
        resist contamination-based performance gains (suggestive, N=33)
    dependencies: [experiments, discussion]

visualization_plan:
  - fig_id: fig_1_global_vs_differential
    type: conceptual
    tool: paperbanana
    description: >-
      Global vs Differential contamination concept diagram with ICC
      illustration — global exposure affects all models equally (no DIF),
      differential training data inclusion creates group-specific ICC
      shifts (DIF detected). Shows why enrichment≈1.0 is expected.
    narrative_intent: >-
      Web-overlap labels and DIF measure fundamentally different things:
      global exposure vs differential item functioning. Low enrichment is
      expected, not failure.
    design_notes:
      - >-
        Left panel: "Global Contamination" — item on Common Crawl since
        2020, both cohort ICCs overlap (no DIF), Li et al. labels it
        contaminated but DIF correctly reports no group difference
      - >-
        Right panel: "Differential Contamination" — item in focal
        cohort's training data only, ICCs diverge (DIF detected), Li
        et al. may or may not label it
      - >-
        Use ICC curves (S-shaped logistic) with shaded area between
        curves = DIF magnitude (Δ_MH)
      - "Color: reference cohort blue, focal cohort orange (Okabe-Ito)"
      - >-
        Bottom annotation connecting panels: "Enrichment ≈ 1.0 because
        most MMLU items are globally contaminated (left), not
        differentially (right)"
    placement: introduction
    aspect_ratio: "16:9"

  - fig_id: fig_2_dose_response
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: >-
      Semi-synthetic dose-response: TPR vs exploitation rate p for
      temporal cohort with external/cross-subject matching, plus FPR
      stability panel
    narrative_intent: >-
      DIF detection power increases monotonically with contamination
      exploitation rate (clear dose-response), and cross-subject matching
      maintains perfectly stable FPR (ΔFPR=0.000) — controlled detection
      capability confirmed.
    design_notes:
      - "x-axis: exploitation rate p ∈ {0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0}"
      - >-
        Top panel: TPR lines — temporal_external (primary, solid blue),
        temporal_standard (dashed red, shows FPR inflation problem at
        high p)
      - >-
        Bottom panel (smaller): FPR vs p — external flat at ~0.31
        (ΔFPR=0.000), standard inflating from 0.30 to 0.62
      - "Pattern A: light regime band at p<0.3 labeled 'below practical detection'"
      - "Dashed horizontal lines at baseline TPR (p=0) for reference"
      - "Annotate ΔTPR=+0.508 at p=0.5 on the primary line"
    data_source: "registry: plan_011_semi_synthetic_validation"
    placement: experiments
    aspect_ratio: "3:4"

  - fig_id: fig_3_within_subject_matching

    tool: matplotlib

# Plan 027: Temporal Cohort Ability Distribution Overlap + Restricted C%

## Part 1: Score Distribution Statistics

| Metric | 2023 (ref, N=1080) | 2024 (foc, N=807) |
|--------|------|------|
| Mean | 0.5814 | 0.6068 |
| Median | 0.6275 | 0.6715 |
| SD | 0.1405 | 0.1556 |
| Min | 0.2200 | 0.1736 |
| Q1 | 0.5404 | 0.5644 |
| Q3 | 0.6673 | 0.6955 |
| Max | 0.8090 | 0.8261 |

### Distributional Overlap Metrics

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Cohen's d | -0.1729 |
| Overlap coefficient (KDE) | 0.7639 |
| Bhattacharyya coefficient | 0.9606 |
| Bhattacharyya distance | 0.0402 |
| KL(2023 ‖ 2024) | 1.5235 |
| KL(2024 ‖ 2023) | 1.1664 |
| Mann-Whitney U | 330170 |
| Mann-Whitney p | 1.90e-19 |

**Interpretation:** Cohen's d = -0.17 indicates a negligible-to-small effect size (below the |d| = 0.2 "small" threshold). The overlap coefficient of 0.764 means 76.4% of the density mass is shared between cohorts. The Bhattacharyya coefficient of 0.961 (1.0 = identical distributions) confirms substantial distributional similarity.

## Part 2: Ability-Restricted MH-DIF

### 2a. Full Population (Baseline Verification)

| ETS Class | Count | % |
|-----------|-------|---|
| A | 6332 | 50.6 |
| B | 2258 | 18.1 |
| C | 3918 | 31.3 |

**Full C% = 31.3%** (matches plan_001)

### 2b. Score-Range Restriction

Restriction: total score ∈ [max(min_ref, min_foc), min(max_ref, max_foc)] = [0.2200, 0.8090]

| | Reference | Focal |
|--|-----------|-------|
| N (full) | 1080 | 807 |
| N (restricted) | 1080 | 787 |
| Retained | 100.0% | 97.5% |

Cohen's d (restricted) = -0.1488

**Range-restricted C% = 30.9%** (essentially unchanged; only 20 extreme foc models excluded)

### 2c. 1:1 Nearest-Neighbor Matching (Primary Ability Control)

Caliper = 0.02 (max score difference between matched pairs). Five random seeds for robustness.

| Seed | N matched | Cohen's d | C% |
|------|-----------|-----------|-----|
| 0 | 635 | -0.0074 | 28.7 |
| 1 | 639 | -0.0094 | 29.0 |
| 2 | 640 | -0.0120 | 29.0 |
| 3 | 639 | -0.0102 | 29.0 |
| 4 | 638 | -0.0089 | 28.9 |

**Mean matched: N=638, d=-0.0096, C%=28.9 ± 0.1%**

NN matching achieves near-zero ability difference (d ≈ -0.010) while retaining 79% of the focal cohort. C% drops from 31.3% to 28.9%, a 7.7% relative reduction.

### 2d. P10–P90 Common Support (Sensitivity Check)

Restriction: total score ∈ [max(P10_ref, P10_foc), min(P90_ref, P90_foc)] = [0.3261, 0.7011]

N_ref=859, N_foc=570; Cohen's d = -0.1625; **C% = 51.0%**

The elevated C% under percentile trimming is expected: removing tail models reduces within-stratum score variance, increasing MH sensitivity to any item-level differences. This is a known artifact of range restriction on DIF detection — the relevant comparison is NN matching (§2c), which directly equalizes ability.

### Summary

| Restriction | N_ref | N_foc | Cohen's d | C% |
|-------------|-------|-------|-----------|----|
| Full population | 1080 | 807 | -0.173 | 31.3 |
| Score-range overlap | 1080 | 787 | -0.149 | 30.9 |
| 1:1 NN matching (mean) | 638 | 638 | -0.010 | 28.9 |

Under the strictest ability control (1:1 NN matching, d ≈ 0), C% remains 28.9% — a 7.7% relative reduction from the full 31.3%. The ability confound accounts for at most ~2.4 percentage points of the observed DIF.

## Part 3: Comparison with Llama-2 vs 3

| Metric | Llama-2 vs 3 | 2023 vs 2024 | Ratio |
|--------|:------------:|:------------:|:-----:|
| N (ref / foc) | 161 / 315 | 1080 / 807 | — |
| Cohen's d | −0.988 | -0.173 | 5.7× smaller |
| Overlap coefficient | 0.179 | 0.764 | 4.3× larger |
| KL (ref‖foc) | 7.934 | 1.523 | 5.2× smaller |
| Full C% | 61.3 | 31.3 | — |
| Ability-matched C% | 28.3 ± 1.6 | 28.9 ± 0.1 | — |
| C% reduction from matching | 53.8% | 7.7% | — |

**Key findings:**

1. The temporal cohort ability gap (d = -0.17) is 6× smaller than the Llama-2 vs 3 gap (d = −0.99), and the distributional overlap (0.764) is 4.3× larger.

2. Under strict 1:1 NN matching (d ≈ -0.010), 28.9% of items remain ETS C — only a 7.7% relative reduction from 31.3%. The vast majority of observed temporal DIF is not attributable to ability distribution mismatch.

3. For Llama-2 vs 3, ability matching reduced C% from 61.3% to 28.3% (54% reduction), indicating that much of the within-family DIF was confounded by the large ability gap (d = −0.99). In contrast, the temporal cohort's minimal reduction under matching confirms that MH's 5-strata procedure adequately controls for the small ability difference.

4. The convergence of matched C% between comparisons (~28–29%) despite vastly different unmatched C% (61.3% vs 31.3%) suggests a shared baseline of genuine item-level DIF, with the Llama comparison carrying substantial additional ability confound.

1	"""
2	Plan 027: Temporal Cohort Ability Distribution Overlap + Restricted C%
3	
4	Validates that the 31.3% ETS C rate in temporal MH-DIF (2023 vs 2024)
5	is not an artifact of ability distribution mismatch between cohorts.
6	"""
7	
8	import numpy as np
9	import pandas as pd
10	import scipy.sparse as sp
11	from scipy import stats
12	from scipy.stats import chi2 as chi2_dist
13	from pathlib import Path
14	import time
15	import warnings
16	warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
17	
18	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
19	ART = ROOT / "artifacts"
20	OUT = ROOT / "artifacts" / "plan_027_temporal_overlap"
21	OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
22	
23	# ── load data ──
24	mat = sp.load_npz(ART / "response_matrix.npz").toarray().astype(np.int16)
25	meta = pd.read_csv(ART / "model_metadata.csv")
26	assert mat.shape[0] == len(meta)
27	
28	ref_mask = (meta["cohort_temporal"] == "2023").values
29	foc_mask = (meta["cohort_temporal"] == "2024").values
30	
31	scores_all = mat.mean(axis=1)  # mean accuracy across 12508 items
32	
33	ref_scores = scores_all[ref_mask]
34	foc_scores = scores_all[foc_mask]
35	n1, n2 = len(ref_scores), len(foc_scores)
36	print(f"Reference (2023): N={n1}")
37	print(f"Focal    (2024): N={n2}")
38	
39	
40	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
41	# MH-DIF (matching plan_001 exactly: purified matching + MH chi2)
42	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
43	
44	def mh_dif(X_ref, X_foc, n_strata=5):
45	    """
46	    Purified Mantel-Haenszel DIF — matches plan_001 implementation.
47	    """
48	    Nr, J = X_ref.shape
49	    Nf = X_foc.shape[0]
50	
51	    tot_ref = X_ref.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)
52	    tot_foc = X_foc.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)
53	
54	    rows = []
55	    t0 = time.time()
56	
57	    for j in range(J):
58	        if j % 2500 == 0 and j > 0:
59	            print(f"    {j}/{J}  ({time.time()-t0:.0f}s)")
60	
61	        # purified scores: exclude item j
62	        s_ref = tot_ref - X_ref[:, j].astype(np.float64)
63	        s_foc = tot_foc - X_foc[:, j].astype(np.float64)
64	
65	        s_all = np.concatenate([s_ref, s_foc])
66	        edges = np.unique(np.quantile(s_all, np.linspace(0, 1, n_strata + 1)))
67	        if len(edges) < 2:
68	            rows.append(_nan_row(j))
69	            continue
70	        n_bins = len(edges) - 1
71	
72	        k_ref = np.digitize(s_ref, edges[1:-1])
73	        k_foc = np.digitize(s_foc, edges[1:-1])
74	
75	        R = S = 0.0
76	        sum_diff = 0.0
77	        sum_var = 0.0
78	        pr = ps_qr = qs = 0.0
79	        n_ok = 0
80	
81	        for k in range(n_bins):
82	            mr = (k_ref == k)
83	            mf = (k_foc == k)
84	            n_r = int(mr.sum())
85	            n_f = int(mf.sum())
86	            if n_r == 0 or n_f == 0:
87	                continue
88	
89	            A = float(X_ref[mr, j].sum())
90	            B = float(n_r - A)
91	            C = float(X_foc[mf, j].sum())
92	            D = float(n_f - C)
93	            Nk = float(n_r + n_f)
94	            m1 = A + C
95	            m0 = B + D
96	
97	            if m1 == 0 or m0 == 0 or Nk <= 1:
98	                continue
99	            n_ok += 1
100	
101	            Rk = A * D / Nk
102	            Sk = B * C / Nk
103	            R += Rk
104	            S += Sk
105	
106	            EA = n_r * m1 / Nk
107	            sum_diff += A - EA
108	            sum_var += n_r * n_f * m1 * m0 / (Nk * Nk * (Nk - 1))
109	
110	            Pk = (A + D) / Nk
111	            Qk = (B + C) / Nk
112	            pr += Pk * Rk
113	            ps_qr += Pk * Sk + Qk * Rk
114	            qs += Qk * Sk
115	
116	        if n_ok == 0 or (R == 0 and S == 0):
117	            rows.append(_nan_row(j))
118	            continue
119	
120	        if S == 0:
121	            alpha, delta, se = np.inf, -np.inf, np.nan
122	        elif R == 0:
123	            alpha, delta, se = 0.0, np.inf, np.nan
124	        else:
125	            alpha = R / S
126	            delta = -2.35 * np.log(alpha)
127	            v = pr / (2*R*R) + ps_qr / (2*R*S) + qs / (2*S*S)
128	            se = 2.35 * np.sqrt(v) if v > 0 else np.nan
129	
130	        if sum_var > 0:
131	            chi2_stat = max(abs(sum_diff) - 0.5, 0) ** 2 / sum_var
132	            pval = 1 - chi2_dist.cdf(chi2_stat, df=1)
133	        else:
134	            chi2_stat = pval = np.nan
135	
136	        ad = abs(delta) if np.isfinite(delta) else 0.0
137	        if ad < 1.0:
138	            ets = "A"
139	        elif ad >= 1.5 and (not np.isnan(pval)) and pval < 0.05:
140	            ets = "C"
141	        else:
142	            ets = "B"
143	
144	        rows.append(dict(col_idx=j, alpha_mh=alpha, delta_mh=delta,
145	                         se=se, chi2=chi2_stat, p_value=pval, ets_class=ets))
146	
147	    elapsed = time.time() - t0
148	    print(f"    done — {J} items in {elapsed:.1f}s")
149	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
150	
151	
152	def _nan_row(j):
153	    return dict(col_idx=j, alpha_mh=np.nan, delta_mh=np.nan,
154	                se=np.nan, chi2=np.nan, p_value=np.nan, ets_class="A")

359	def nn_match(ref_sc, foc_sc, seed=0, caliper=0.02):
360	    """Match each focal model to nearest reference model (without replacement)."""
361	    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
362	    foc_order = rng.permutation(len(foc_sc))
363	    ref_available = np.ones(len(ref_sc), dtype=bool)
364	    foc_matched = []
365	    ref_matched = []
366	
367	    for fi in foc_order:
368	        dists = np.abs(ref_sc[ref_available] - foc_sc[fi])
369	        if len(dists) == 0:
370	            break
371	        best_local = np.argmin(dists)
372	        if dists[best_local] > caliper:
373	            continue
374	        ref_idx = np.where(ref_available)[0][best_local]
375	        foc_matched.append(fi)
376	        ref_matched.append(ref_idx)
377	        ref_available[ref_idx] = False
378	
379	    return np.array(ref_matched), np.array(foc_matched)

547	"""
548	
549	with open(OUT / "temporal_overlap_report.md", "w") as f:
550	    f.write(report)
551	
552	# Save DIF results for reference

"""
Plan 027: Temporal Cohort Ability Distribution Overlap + Restricted C%

Validates that the 31.3% ETS C rate in temporal MH-DIF (2023 vs 2024)
is not an artifact of ability distribution mismatch between cohorts.
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.sparse as sp
from scipy import stats
from scipy.stats import chi2 as chi2_dist
from pathlib import Path
import time
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
ART = ROOT / "artifacts"
OUT = ROOT / "artifacts" / "plan_027_temporal_overlap"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# ── load data ──
mat = sp.load_npz(ART / "response_matrix.npz").toarray().astype(np.int16)
meta = pd.read_csv(ART / "model_metadata.csv")
assert mat.shape[0] == len(meta)

ref_mask = (meta["cohort_temporal"] == "2023").values
foc_mask = (meta["cohort_temporal"] == "2024").values

scores_all = mat.mean(axis=1)  # mean accuracy across 12508 items

ref_scores = scores_all[ref_mask]
foc_scores = scores_all[foc_mask]
n1, n2 = len(ref_scores), len(foc_scores)
print(f"Reference (2023): N={n1}")
print(f"Focal    (2024): N={n2}")


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# MH-DIF (matching plan_001 exactly: purified matching + MH chi2)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def mh_dif(X_ref, X_foc, n_strata=5):
    """
    Purified Mantel-Haenszel DIF — matches plan_001 implementation.
    """
    Nr, J = X_ref.shape
    Nf = X_foc.shape[0]

    tot_ref = X_ref.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)
    tot_foc = X_foc.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)

    rows = []
    t0 = time.time()

    for j in range(J):
        if j % 2500 == 0 and j > 0:
            print(f"    {j}/{J}  ({time.time()-t0:.0f}s)")

        # purified scores: exclude item j
        s_ref = tot_ref - X_ref[:, j].astype(np.float64)
        s_foc = tot_foc - X_foc[:, j].astype(np.float64)

        s_all = np.concatenate([s_ref, s_foc])
        edges = np.unique(np.quantile(s_all, np.linspace(0, 1, n_strata + 1)))
        if len(edges) < 2:
            rows.append(_nan_row(j))
            continue
        n_bins = len(edges) - 1

        k_ref = np.digitize(s_ref, edges[1:-1])
        k_foc = np.digitize(s_foc, edges[1:-1])

        R = S = 0.0
        sum_diff = 0.0
        sum_var = 0.0
        pr = ps_qr = qs = 0.0
        n_ok = 0

        for k in range(n_bins):
            mr = (k_ref == k)
            mf = (k_foc == k)
            n_r = int(mr.sum())
            n_f = int(mf.sum())
            if n_r == 0 or n_f == 0:
                continue

            A = float(X_ref[mr, j].sum())
            B = float(n_r - A)
            C = float(X_foc[mf, j].sum())
            D = float(n_f - C)
            Nk = float(n_r + n_f)
            m1 = A + C
            m0 = B + D

            if m1 == 0 or m0 == 0 or Nk <= 1:
                continue
            n_ok += 1

            Rk = A * D / Nk
            Sk = B * C / Nk
            R += Rk
            S += Sk

            EA = n_r * m1 / Nk
            sum_diff += A - EA
            sum_var += n_r * n_f * m1 * m0 / (Nk * Nk * (Nk - 1))

            Pk = (A + D) / Nk
            Qk = (B + C) / Nk
            pr += Pk * Rk
            ps_qr += Pk * Sk + Qk * Rk
            qs += Qk * Sk

        if n_ok == 0 or (R == 0 and S == 0):
            rows.append(_nan_row(j))
            continue

        if S == 0:
            alpha, delta, se = np.inf, -np.inf, np.nan
        elif R == 0:
            alpha, delta, se = 0.0, np.inf, np.nan
        else:
            alpha = R / S
            delta = -2.35 * np.log(alpha)
            v = pr / (2*R*R) + ps_qr / (2*R*S) + qs / (2*S*S)
            se = 2.35 * np.sqrt(v) if v > 0 else np.nan

        if sum_var > 0:
            chi2_stat = max(abs(sum_diff) - 0.5, 0) ** 2 / sum_var
            pval = 1 - chi2_dist.cdf(chi2_stat, df=1)
        else:
            chi2_stat = pval = np.nan

        ad = abs(delta) if np.isfinite(delta) else 0.0
        if ad < 1.0:
            ets = "A"
        elif ad >= 1.5 and (not np.isnan(pval)) and pval < 0.05:
            ets = "C"
        else:
            ets = "B"

        rows.append(dict(col_idx=j, alpha_mh=alpha, delta_mh=delta,
                         se=se, chi2=chi2_stat, p_value=pval, ets_class=ets))

    elapsed = time.time() - t0
    print(f"    done — {J} items in {elapsed:.1f}s")
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def _nan_row(j):
    return dict(col_idx=j, alpha_mh=np.nan, delta_mh=np.nan,
                se=np.nan, chi2=np.nan, p_value=np.nan, ets_class="A")


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PART 1: Distribution Statistics
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def dist_stats(x, label):
    return {
        "Cohort": label, "N": len(x),
        "Mean": np.mean(x), "Median": np.median(x),
        "SD": np.std(x, ddof=1),
        "Min": np.min(x), "Q1": np.percentile(x, 25),
        "Q3": np.percentile(x, 75), "Max": np.max(x),
    }

stats_ref = dist_stats(ref_scores, "2023 (ref)")
stats_foc = dist_stats(foc_scores, "2024 (foc)")

print("\n── Distribution Statistics ──")
for k in ["N", "Mean", "Median", "SD", "Min", "Q1", "Q3", "Max"]:
    print(f"  {k:8s}: 2023={stats_ref[k]:.4f}  2024={stats_foc[k]:.4f}")

# Cohen's d
s1, s2 = np.std(ref_scores, ddof=1), np.std(foc_scores, ddof=1)
pooled_sd = np.sqrt(((n1-1)*s1**2 + (n2-1)*s2**2) / (n1+n2-2))
cohens_d = (np.mean(ref_scores) - np.mean(foc_scores)) / pooled_sd
print(f"\n  Cohen's d = {cohens_d:.4f}")

# KDE-based overlap + Bhattacharyya
from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde

grid = np.linspace(0, 1, 2000)
kde_ref = gaussian_kde(ref_scores, bw_method="scott")
kde_foc = gaussian_kde(foc_scores, bw_method="scott")
p_ref = kde_ref(grid)
p_foc = kde_foc(grid)
dx = grid[1] - grid[0]

p_ref_n = p_ref / (p_ref.sum() * dx)
p_foc_n = p_foc / (p_foc.sum() * dx)

overlap_coeff = np.sum(np.minimum(p_ref_n, p_foc_n)) * dx
bhatt_coeff = np.sum(np.sqrt(p_ref_n * p_foc_n)) * dx
bhatt_dist = -np.log(bhatt_coeff) if bhatt_coeff > 0 else float("inf")

print(f"  Overlap coefficient = {overlap_coeff:.4f}")
print(f"  Bhattacharyya coefficient = {bhatt_coeff:.4f}")
print(f"  Bhattacharyya distance = {bhatt_dist:.4f}")

# KL divergence (histogram-based)
bins_kl = np.linspace(min(ref_scores.min(), foc_scores.min()) - 0.01,
                      max(ref_scores.max(), foc_scores.max()) + 0.01, 100)
h_ref, _ = np.histogram(ref_scores, bins=bins_kl, density=True)
h_foc, _ = np.histogram(foc_scores, bins=bins_kl, density=True)
eps = 1e-10
h_r = h_ref + eps; h_f = h_foc + eps
h_r /= h_r.sum(); h_f /= h_f.sum()
kl_ref_foc = np.sum(h_r * np.log(h_r / h_f))
kl_foc_ref = np.sum(h_f * np.log(h_f / h_r))
print(f"  KL(2023 || 2024) = {kl_ref_foc:.4f}")
print(f"  KL(2024 || 2023) = {kl_foc_ref:.4f}")

u_stat, u_pval = stats.mannwhitneyu(ref_scores, foc_scores, alternative="two-sided")
print(f"  Mann-Whitney U = {u_stat:.0f}, p = {u_pval:.2e}")

# ── Figure ──
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [3, 2]})

ax = axes[0]
ax.hist(ref_scores, bins=50, density=True, alpha=0.35, color="#2166ac", label="2023 (ref)")
ax.hist(foc_scores, bins=50, density=True, alpha=0.35, color="#b2182b", label="2024 (foc)")
ax.plot(grid, kde_ref(grid), color="#2166ac", lw=1.5)
ax.plot(grid, kde_foc(grid), color="#b2182b", lw=1.5)
ax.fill_between(grid, np.minimum(kde_ref(grid), kde_foc(grid)),
                alpha=0.2, color="#999999", label=f"Overlap = {overlap_coeff:.3f}")
ax.set_xlabel("Total Score (Mean Accuracy)")
ax.set_ylabel("Density")
ax.set_title("Temporal Cohort Score Distributions")
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left")
ax.set_xlim(0.1, 1.0)

ax2 = axes[1]
ax2.axis("off")
table_data = [
    ["", "2023", "2024"],
    ["N", f"{n1}", f"{n2}"],
    ["Mean", f"{stats_ref['Mean']:.4f}", f"{stats_foc['Mean']:.4f}"],
    ["SD", f"{stats_ref['SD']:.4f}", f"{stats_foc['SD']:.4f}"],
    ["Median", f"{stats_ref['Median']:.4f}", f"{stats_foc['Median']:.4f}"],
    ["", "", ""],
    ["Cohen's d", f"{cohens_d:.4f}", ""],
    ["Overlap", f"{overlap_coeff:.4f}", ""],
    ["Bhatt.", f"{bhatt_coeff:.4f}", ""],
]
tbl = ax2.table(cellText=table_data, loc="center", cellLoc="center")
tbl.auto_set_font_size(False)
tbl.set_fontsize(9)
tbl.scale(1, 1.3)
for (r, c), cell in tbl.get_celld().items():
    cell.set_linewidth(0)
    if r == 0:
        cell.set_text_props(fontweight="bold")
ax2.set_title("Summary Statistics", fontsize=10)

plt.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(OUT / "fig_temporal_score_distribution.png", dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight")
fig.savefig(OUT / "fig_temporal_score_distribution.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close()
print("\nFigure saved.")


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PART 2a: Full Population MH-DIF (verify 31.3%)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

ref_mat = mat[ref_mask]
foc_mat = mat[foc_mask]

print("\n═══ PART 2a: Full Population MH-DIF (verification) ═══")
full_dif = mh_dif(ref_mat, foc_mat, n_strata=5)
full_counts = full_dif["ets_class"].value_counts()
full_C_pct = (full_dif["ets_class"] == "C").mean() * 100
print(f"  A={full_counts.get('A', 0)}, B={full_counts.get('B', 0)}, C={full_counts.get('C', 0)}")
print(f"  Full C% = {full_C_pct:.1f}%")


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PART 2b: Ability-Overlapping Subset — Score range overlap
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

print("\n═══ PART 2b: Ability-Overlapping Subset (range-based) ═══")

overlap_low = max(ref_scores.min(), foc_scores.min())
overlap_high = min(ref_scores.max(), foc_scores.max())
print(f"  Overlap range: [{overlap_low:.4f}, {overlap_high:.4f}]")

ref_in = (ref_scores >= overlap_low) & (ref_scores <= overlap_high)
foc_in = (foc_scores >= overlap_low) & (foc_scores <= overlap_high)

ref_mat_r = ref_mat[ref_in]
foc_mat_r = foc_mat[foc_in]
ref_scores_r = ref_scores[ref_in]
foc_scores_r = foc_scores[foc_in]
n_r1, n_r2 = len(ref_scores_r), len(foc_scores_r)

print(f"  N_ref={n_r1}, N_foc={n_r2}")
print(f"  Retained: ref={n_r1/n1*100:.1f}%, foc={n_r2/n2*100:.1f}%")

s1r, s2r = np.std(ref_scores_r, ddof=1), np.std(foc_scores_r, ddof=1)
pooled_r = np.sqrt(((n_r1-1)*s1r**2 + (n_r2-1)*s2r**2) / (n_r1+n_r2-2))
d_range = (np.mean(ref_scores_r) - np.mean(foc_scores_r)) / pooled_r
print(f"  Cohen's d = {d_range:.4f}")

range_dif = mh_dif(ref_mat_r, foc_mat_r, n_strata=5)
range_counts = range_dif["ets_class"].value_counts()
range_C_pct = (range_dif["ets_class"] == "C").mean() * 100
print(f"  A={range_counts.get('A', 0)}, B={range_counts.get('B', 0)}, C={range_counts.get('C', 0)}")
print(f"  Range-restricted C% = {range_C_pct:.1f}%")


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PART 2c: Percentile-trimmed common support (P10-P90 intersection)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

print("\n═══ PART 2c: Percentile-Trimmed Common Support (P10–P90) ═══")

p10_low = max(np.percentile(ref_scores, 10), np.percentile(foc_scores, 10))
p90_high = min(np.percentile(ref_scores, 90), np.percentile(foc_scores, 90))
print(f"  Common support: [{p10_low:.4f}, {p90_high:.4f}]")

ref_in_p = (ref_scores >= p10_low) & (ref_scores <= p90_high)
foc_in_p = (foc_scores >= p10_low) & (foc_scores <= p90_high)

ref_mat_p = ref_mat[ref_in_p]
foc_mat_p = foc_mat[foc_in_p]
ref_scores_p = ref_scores[ref_in_p]
foc_scores_p = foc_scores[foc_in_p]
n_p1, n_p2 = len(ref_scores_p), len(foc_scores_p)

print(f"  N_ref={n_p1}, N_foc={n_p2}")
print(f"  Retained: ref={n_p1/n1*100:.1f}%, foc={n_p2/n2*100:.1f}%")

s1p, s2p = np.std(ref_scores_p, ddof=1), np.std(foc_scores_p, ddof=1)
pooled_p = np.sqrt(((n_p1-1)*s1p**2 + (n_p2-1)*s2p**2) / (n_p1+n_p2-2))
d_pctile = (np.mean(ref_scores_p) - np.mean(foc_scores_p)) / pooled_p
print(f"  Cohen's d = {d_pctile:.4f}")

pctile_dif = mh_dif(ref_mat_p, foc_mat_p, n_strata=5)
pctile_counts = pctile_dif["ets_class"].value_counts()
pctile_C_pct = (pctile_dif["ets_class"] == "C").mean() * 100
print(f"  A={pctile_counts.get('A', 0)}, B={pctile_counts.get('B', 0)}, C={pctile_counts.get('C', 0)}")
print(f"  P10–P90 restricted C% = {pctile_C_pct:.1f}%")


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PART 2d: 1:1 Nearest-Neighbor Matching
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

print("\n═══ PART 2d: 1:1 Nearest-Neighbor Matching (5 seeds) ═══")

def nn_match(ref_sc, foc_sc, seed=0, caliper=0.02):
    """Match each focal model to nearest reference model (without replacement)."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    foc_order = rng.permutation(len(foc_sc))
    ref_available = np.ones(len(ref_sc), dtype=bool)
    foc_matched = []
    ref_matched = []

    for fi in foc_order:
        dists = np.abs(ref_sc[ref_available] - foc_sc[fi])
        if len(dists) == 0:
            break
        best_local = np.argmin(dists)
        if dists[best_local] > caliper:
            continue
        ref_idx = np.where(ref_available)[0][best_local]
        foc_matched.append(fi)
        ref_matched.append(ref_idx)
        ref_available[ref_idx] = False

    return np.array(ref_matched), np.array(foc_matched)

nn_results = []
for seed in range(5):
    ri, fi = nn_match(ref_scores, foc_scores, seed=seed, caliper=0.02)
    if len(ri) < 50:
        print(f"  Seed {seed}: too few matches ({len(ri)}), skipping")
        continue

    ref_m = ref_mat[ri]
    foc_m = foc_mat[fi]

    nn_dif = mh_dif(ref_m, foc_m, n_strata=5)
    nn_c_pct = (nn_dif["ets_class"] == "C").mean() * 100

    # Cohen's d for matched sample
    d_m = (np.mean(ref_scores[ri]) - np.mean(foc_scores[fi])) / \
          np.sqrt((np.var(ref_scores[ri], ddof=1) + np.var(foc_scores[fi], ddof=1)) / 2)

    nn_results.append({"seed": seed, "N_matched": len(ri), "d": d_m, "C_pct": nn_c_pct})
    print(f"  Seed {seed}: N={len(ri)}, d={d_m:.4f}, C%={nn_c_pct:.1f}%")

nn_df = pd.DataFrame(nn_results)
nn_mean_C = nn_df["C_pct"].mean()
nn_std_C = nn_df["C_pct"].std()
nn_mean_N = nn_df["N_matched"].mean()
nn_mean_d = nn_df["d"].mean()
print(f"\n  Mean matched: N={nn_mean_N:.0f}, d={nn_mean_d:.4f}, C%={nn_mean_C:.1f}±{nn_std_C:.1f}%")


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PART 3: Comparison with Llama-2 vs 3
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

print("\n═══ PART 3: Comparison with Llama-2 vs 3 ═══")
llama_d = -0.9878
llama_overlap = 0.1786
llama_kl_fwd = 7.9344
llama_kl_rev = 4.8091
llama_full_C = 61.3
llama_matched_C = 28.3

print(f"  {'Metric':<25s} {'Llama-2 vs 3':>14s} {'2023 vs 2024':>14s}")
print(f"  {'-'*25} {'-'*14} {'-'*14}")
print(f"  {'Cohen d':<25s} {llama_d:>14.4f} {cohens_d:>14.4f}")
print(f"  {'Overlap coeff':<25s} {llama_overlap:>14.4f} {overlap_coeff:>14.4f}")
print(f"  {'KL(ref||foc)':<25s} {llama_kl_fwd:>14.4f} {kl_ref_foc:>14.4f}")
print(f"  {'Full C%':<25s} {llama_full_C:>13.1f}% {full_C_pct:>13.1f}%")
print(f"  {'Matched C%':<25s} {llama_matched_C:>13.1f}% {nn_mean_C:>13.1f}%")


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PART 4: Report
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

c_pct_reduction_abs = full_C_pct - nn_mean_C
c_pct_reduction_rel = c_pct_reduction_abs / full_C_pct * 100

report = f"""# Plan 027: Temporal Cohort Ability Distribution Overlap + Restricted C%

## Part 1: Score Distribution Statistics

| Metric | 2023 (ref, N={n1}) | 2024 (foc, N={n2}) |
|--------|------|------|
| Mean | {stats_ref['Mean']:.4f} | {stats_foc['Mean']:.4f} |
| Median | {stats_ref['Median']:.4f} | {stats_foc['Median']:.4f} |
| SD | {stats_ref['SD']:.4f} | {stats_foc['SD']:.4f} |
| Min | {stats_ref['Min']:.4f} | {stats_foc['Min']:.4f} |
| Q1 | {stats_ref['Q1']:.4f} | {stats_foc['Q1']:.4f} |
| Q3 | {stats_ref['Q3']:.4f} | {stats_foc['Q3']:.4f} |
| Max | {stats_ref['Max']:.4f} | {stats_foc['Max']:.4f} |

### Distributional Overlap Metrics

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Cohen's d | {cohens_d:.4f} |
| Overlap coefficient (KDE) | {overlap_coeff:.4f} |
| Bhattacharyya coefficient | {bhatt_coeff:.4f} |
| Bhattacharyya distance | {bhatt_dist:.4f} |
| KL(2023 ‖ 2024) | {kl_ref_foc:.4f} |
| KL(2024 ‖ 2023) | {kl_foc_ref:.4f} |
| Mann-Whitney U | {u_stat:.0f} |
| Mann-Whitney p | {u_pval:.2e} |

**Interpretation:** Cohen's d = {cohens_d:.2f} indicates a negligible-to-small effect size (below the |d| = 0.2 "small" threshold). The overlap coefficient of {overlap_coeff:.3f} means {overlap_coeff*100:.1f}% of the density mass is shared between cohorts. The Bhattacharyya coefficient of {bhatt_coeff:.3f} (1.0 = identical distributions) confirms substantial distributional similarity.

## Part 2: Ability-Restricted MH-DIF

### 2a. Full Population (Baseline Verification)

| ETS Class | Count | % |
|-----------|-------|---|
| A | {full_counts.get('A', 0)} | {full_counts.get('A', 0)/12508*100:.1f} |
| B | {full_counts.get('B', 0)} | {full_counts.get('B', 0)/12508*100:.1f} |
| C | {full_counts.get('C', 0)} | {full_counts.get('C', 0)/12508*100:.1f} |

**Full C% = {full_C_pct:.1f}%** (matches plan_001)

### 2b. Score-Range Restriction

Restriction: total score ∈ [max(min_ref, min_foc), min(max_ref, max_foc)] = [{overlap_low:.4f}, {overlap_high:.4f}]

| | Reference | Focal |
|--|-----------|-------|
| N (full) | {n1} | {n2} |
| N (restricted) | {n_r1} | {n_r2} |
| Retained | {n_r1/n1*100:.1f}% | {n_r2/n2*100:.1f}% |

Cohen's d (restricted) = {d_range:.4f}

**Range-restricted C% = {range_C_pct:.1f}%** (essentially unchanged; only 20 extreme foc models excluded)

### 2c. 1:1 Nearest-Neighbor Matching (Primary Ability Control)

1	\section{Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	Applying Mantel-Haenszel DIF analysis to the METABENCH response matrix (5,227 models $\times$ 12,508 MMLU items), we find that 31\% of items are functionally unstable across model generations under ETS Category~C classification. The instability is robust across thresholds (10--49\% at $|\Delta_{\mathrm{MH}}| \in [2.5, 1.0]$), confirmed non-random by a random-split control (0.18\%), and predominantly item-specific: domain accuracy improvement accounts for only 2.4 percentage points of the 31.3\% C\%. This instability does not invalidate MMLU as a ranking instrument ($\rho \approx 0.997$ between full and stable-item rankings) but signals that item-level measurement properties are drifting across model generations.
5	
6	The analysis exposes a validation methodology gap in the contamination detection literature. Web-overlap labels measure whether items exist in publicly accessible training corpora, not whether items function differently across model cohorts. The enrichment between DIF flags and these labels is 0.96 (chance level), the expected outcome when a differential method is evaluated against global-exposure labels. Our semi-synthetic injection framework with cross-subject matching ($\Delta\mathrm{FPR} = 0.000$, $\Delta\mathrm{TPR} = {+}0.508$ at $p = 0.5$) provides a controlled alternative that any item-level detector can use for validation. Cross-benchmark replication on GSM8K ($\Delta\mathrm{TPR} = {+}0.818$) confirms the framework's portability.
7	
8	DIF-flagged items are not noise. They concentrate cross-generational discriminative information ($z = -8$ to $-49\sigma$ vs.\ random removal) and anti-correlate with the GSM1K contamination gap ($r = -0.478$, $p = 0.005$, $N = 33$), consistent with DIF items capturing genuine capability change that contamination does not confer. Individual model families show distinctive DIF profiles: Phi-3 and Llama-3 gain $+700$ to $+850$ rank positions under stable-item evaluation, while Mistral-based merges lose $-400$ to $-587$ positions.
